blocker.summary: The r399 allocator double-issue is RESOLVED (r413/r414/r415, see git log for the full mechanism: r366's own invented critical-section fix in sub_821FA9E0 clobbered its own return value, silently discarding every C++ static-initializer array growth and causing an unbounded heap overflow masked by a -1-sentinel/unsigned-compare defect in the capacity check; fixed and live-verified, r398's exact original repro no longer double-issues). r416 then found sub_821D5F48 returning and sub_821D7AE0/sub_821D7CD0 (the per-frame loop) being entered for the first time in the whole r358-r415 campaign, but only captured 2 hits over up to 120s and framed the subsequent 'generated entry terminated its own thread' message as a possible new blocker. r417 CORRECTS this: sub_821D7DE0 (the loop's caller) is read in full and is an unconditionally infinite loop (bare `goto` back to the top, no exit condition) -- no bug there. A wait-call breakpoint filtered to this loop's own call chain (via sub_82331E78, called directly from sub_821D7DE0 every iteration, not through sub_821D5F48) captured 292 hits over a 5s window with a near-constant ~16-17ms period -- a realistic per-frame cadence, not a stall. The 'terminated its own thread' message is DESIGNED, INTENTIONAL shutdown behavior from r277 (confirmed in tools/materialize_native_import_stubs.py: generated wait stubs check native_guest_threads_stop_requested() and throw ac6::native::GuestThreadTerminated on it, precisely to avoid the SIGSEGV-on-exit r277 documented and fixed) -- it fires when the probe harness's own window elapses and asks guest threads to stop cleanly, not when the game gets stuck. So there is currently NO known blocker in the allocator chain, the boot sequence, or the per-frame loop's own execution. presented_frames still reads 0 despite the per-frame loop visibly running at a realistic cadence -- named for r418: read sub_821D7AE0/sub_821D7CD0 (never read yet) to find where/whether presented_frames should increment and why it doesn't, most likely because this probe-entry harness runs headless with no real display surface rather than any remaining bug in the r399-r415 chain. One loose end also named for r418, not yet investigated: r416's own capture only saw sub_821D7AE0/sub_821D7CD0 entered twice over up to 120s, apparently contradicting r417's 292 hits on the same loop's sub_82331E78 call over just 5s -- check whether r416's script (r425_boot_progress.gdb) has a breakpoint-scoping artifact (it logged a 'Thread-specific breakpoint ... deleted' message that was never investigated) before drawing any conclusion about the real relative frequency of these two functions. The standing uncommitted-tree situation (r239+, over the 2026-09-02 mass deletion) remains the user's decision, untouched -- reports and named tool scripts for r413-r417 were committed individually, the broader tree state was not.
